all_leads.name: Paul Malott (CEO Automations24) + Johnny Halife (CTO Southworks)
all_leads.problem_summary: When a user asks a simple question, the agent interprets it as an execution task and compute costs compound before anyone in finance sees the request. Claude Code users report unexpected token burn just from asking questions. Cost is now tied to autonomous system behavior, not human spending decisions.

all_leads.name: aisaasbuilder (HN user)
all_leads.problem_summary: Most teams see only a monthly AI total, not per-agent or per-step cost attribution. The decision math for AI vs SWE spend only works if both sides of the equation are real numbers. Building traeco.dev to close this gap.

all_leads.name: HN discussion on agents spending money
all_leads.problem_summary: Community consensus: agents proposing actions with cost estimates, humans approving via notification, prepaid virtual cards with low limits. Trust threshold for autonomous agent spending is around $500 in API credits vs e-commerce.
all_leads.dollar_amount: $500 trust threshold for autonomous agent spending

all_leads.name: avaer (HN user)
all_leads.problem_summary: People running 15 agents to write software could use 1-2 with a better multi-page prompt for the same results at a fraction of the cost. Modern agentic coding tools spin up sub-agents on their own — the AI bill goes 'BRR.'

all_leads.name: Nevermined
all_leads.problem_summary: Traditional seat-based pricing fails when a single conversation triggers hundreds of micro-activities with sub-cent costs, making unit economics nearly impossible to track. Need AI-native billing for variable compute costs, sub-cent micro-transactions, and agent-to-agent payments.
